channel.title: WSJ | World
channel.description: WSJ World News RSS, without Opinions

item.title: Trump Says He Would Be Open to Meeting With Putin and Xi
item.description: The president said he would be willing to discuss denuclearization with the leaders of Russia and China.

item.title: Oil Futures Pull Back as U.S. Waives Some Russia Sanctions
item.description: Oil futures fell, pulling back from Friday’s gains after President Trump waived newly imposed sanctions on Russia, while persistent Middle East supply risks kept prices afloat.

item.title: The New Wild West of Gold Mining Is West Africa
item.description: Mining companies have invested billions of dollars in new gold mines to cash in on near-record-high prices for the metal.

item.title: Young Protesters Are Putting India’s Modi on the Defensive
item.description: Narendra Modi’s government has a reputation for being heavy-handed toward dissent, but its tactics in recent days have been met with a mix of wit and defiance by young protesters.

item.title: Former OpenAI Worker Accused of Bugging Discussed Jobs With Saudi Royal
item.description: In a detention filing, prosecutors argue Abdulrahman Alfozan is a flight risk, saying his wife and child moved permanently to Saudi Arabia.

item.title: Israel’s Front-Runners Shun Arab Voters Who Could Help Them Win Election
item.description: Opinion polls suggest the election is deadlocked, except for about a million Arab voters whose backing comes with drawbacks in a polarized society.

item.title: Rioting in France: What’s Fueling the Violence and What Happens Next
item.description: Weeks of student-led protests over conditions in French schools spiraled into violent protests across the country in recent days.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Postpones ‘Davos in the Desert’ Event Slated for Next Week
item.description: The conference will be delayed until 2027, following attacks by the Iran-backed Houthis on the kingdom’s airports.

item.title: KKR Sent Formal Objection by EU Over Information Provided in NetCo Deal
item.description: The European Commission said it provisionally found that the group gave what it said was incorrect or misleading information related to long-term wholesale access agreements.

item.title: French Leaders Trade Blame After Rioting Sweeps the Nation
item.description: Police struggled to contain groups that attacked everything from city halls to luxury boutiques.

item.title: Putin Floats a Summit With Trump and Xi to Discuss Ukraine Deal
item.description: Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelensky wouldn’t be included in the proposed talks, as Russia’s leader seeks to negotiate an end to the war that favors Moscow.

item.title: China’s Export Boom Masks Deep Economic Problems at Home
item.description: Even as China makes strides in areas such as AI, much of its domestic economy is dragged down by gloomy consumer sentiment and a real-estate slump.

item.title: French Contagion Less Virulent Than in Previous Eurozone Crisis
item.description: The eurozone has learned some lessons from its last debt crisis, the bloc is unlikely to suffer a repeat of that traumatic episode as France wrestles its debt problems.

item.title: China’s Economy Expanded 4.5% in Third Quarter, Powered by Exports
item.description: Economic growth accelerated, though consumer confidence and property market woes persist.

item.title: Saudi Arabia’s Military Limitations Are Being Exposed by Houthi Attacks
item.description: The kingdom has advanced weaponry, but the Yemeni militant group has proved to be a resilient foe.

item.title: Trump’s Overtures to Putin Put Republican Candidates in Hot Seat
item.description: GOP politicians in a number of tight races are breaking with Trump on Russia policy ahead of midterms.

item.title: Wall Street Elite Can’t Decide How to RSVP to the Prince’s Big Saudi Conference
item.description: Recent attacks by Houthi rebels are making U.S. executives nervous to travel to the Future Investment Initiative conference in Saudi Arabia next week.

item.title: Trump Endorses Israel’s Netanyahu for Re-Election
item.description: The embattled Israeli leader had long sought Trump’s backing in tight elections scheduled for this month.

item.title: Ukrainian Drone Strike Hits Putin’s Hometown, Striking Oil Terminal
item.description: The fresh attack on Russian oil facilities came after President Trump’s efforts to enforce a fragile energy ceasefire collapsed.

item.title: Zelensky Takes a Risk by Publicly Confronting Trump Over Russia
item.description: Plus, masked Israeli settlers attack a group of European diplomats, and a playboy inherits the world’s most notorious mercenary force.
